affectedPublicSurfaces: No user-facing route, asset or frontend change. The public-release classification comes from the transport-guard path: `integrations/tiktok/capabilities.py` stops defining its own `PRODUCTION_AUTH_ID`/`SANDBOX_AUTH_ID` literals and sources them from `merchant.py`, which #1234 made environment-configurable. `factories.py`'s `ProductionReadClientFactory` / `SandboxWriteClientFactory` keep their comparison logic unchanged; only the values they compare against stop being compiled-in.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Local tests on feature/issue-1246-capabilities-merchant-config, cut from feature/agent-w4-wave. No VPS contact, no deployment, no vendor calls.

the same holds for SandboxWriteClientFactory and TIKTOK_SANDBOX_MERCHANT_ID

htmlRoutes: No HTML route or asset change — two constants change their source module, plus tests.

migrationCompatibility.notes: No migration, no schema change, no new environment variable. #1234 already introduced TIKTOK_PRODUCTION_MERCHANT_ID and TIKTOK_SANDBOX_MERCHANT_ID; this slice only redirects where two existing constants are read from. Stable and candidate pods agree because both read the same defaults when the vars are unset.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Without this slice, a deployment that sets the two env vars per #1234's own onboarding documentation gets correct classification from merchant.py and then a hard ValueError from ProductionReadClientFactory, because capabilities.py still holds Juli's compiled-in IDs. That is today's accepted, signed-off state (#1234's PASS_WITH_WARNINGS) — no new exposure, but the documented onboarding path stays broken.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Revert the commit; capabilities.py returns to its own literals and behaviour returns to the signed-off #1234 state. The guard semantics are unchanged either way — a mismatched merchant raises ValueError before any client is constructed, so no cross-merchant request can be issued in either direction. The failure mode this slice removes is fail-closed, never a silent misroute, which is why reverting is safe rather than merely tolerable.

acceptanceCommands: PYTHONPATH=$PWD/backend/src python -m pytest tests/unit -q -k 'merchant or capabilit or factor or tiktok_credential'
doNotInfer: This slice does not add, rename or remove an environment variable — #1234 already added both.
It does not change factories.py's comparison logic, only the source of the values compared. A mismatched merchant must still raise.
merchant.py has zero internal juli_backend imports, so sourcing from it introduces no circular-import risk. That was verified before the issue was filed, not assumed.
This does not touch multi-merchant ingest fan-out or rollout, which PLAN.md places in P13 territory.
